_meta.description: Security domain vocabulary for Leviathan. Extends core terms with security-specific concepts.

@threat.definition: Any input, action, or sequence that could cause unintended harm to the host system, user data, or connected services.
categories: data_exfiltration — unauthorized transmission of sensitive data
destructive_command — actions that delete, corrupt, or modify critical resources
privilege_escalation — attempts to gain unauthorized access levels
prompt_injection — malicious instructions hidden in seemingly benign content
supply_chain — compromised dependencies or external resources

severity_levels.CRITICAL: Immediate, irreversible harm (e.g., rm -rf, wallet drain)
severity_levels.HIGH: Significant harm, potentially reversible (e.g., file deletion with backup)
severity_levels.MEDIUM: Limited harm, easily reversible (e.g., config change)
severity_levels.LOW: Minimal harm, informational concern (e.g., verbose logging)
severity_levels.INFO: No harm, but worth noting (e.g., deprecated function)

@action.definition: Any operation an agent attempts to execute on behalf of or affecting the user.
types: shell_execution — running commands in system shell
file_operation — read, write, delete, move files
network_request — HTTP calls, API requests, data transmission
process_control — starting, stopping, or modifying processes
credential_access — reading or using authentication tokens
financial_transaction — any operation involving value transfer
@action.audit_requirement: All actions SHOULD be auditable before execution.

@context.definition: The situational information surrounding an action request.
required_fields: source — where the action request originated (moltbook, email, slack, etc.)
content — the raw content triggering the action
proposed_action — what the agent wants to do
optional_fields: user_intent — what the human user originally asked for
chain_of_thought — agent's reasoning for this action
previous_actions — recent action history for pattern detection

@verdict.definition: The security decision made by the audit system.

outcomes.BLOCK: Action violates security principles, must not execute
outcomes.WARN: Action has risks, proceed with caution and user confirmation
outcomes.SANDBOX: Action should run in isolated environment only

required_fields: outcome — ALLOW, BLOCK, WARN, or SANDBOX
reasoning — explanation of why this decision was made
violated_principles — list of principles that would be violated (if any)

@sandbox.definition: An isolated execution environment that limits the blast radius of potentially harmful actions.

properties.filesystem: Restricted to specific directories, no access to host system
properties.network: Optionally disabled or limited to allowlist
properties.resources: CPU, memory, and time limits enforced
properties.persistence: No state persists after execution unless explicitly saved

@sandbox.note: Default recommendation for untrusted code execution.

@consent.definition: Explicit user approval for an action, especially those with significant impact.

levels.implicit: User's general instructions imply approval (e.g., 'organize my files')
levels.informed: User approves after understanding risks (e.g., 'this will delete files, proceed?')
levels.explicit: User directly commands the specific action (e.g., 'delete file X')

@consent.requirement: CRITICAL and HIGH severity actions require at minimum informed consent.

@audit_trail.definition: A chronological record of all actions attempted, their verdicts, and outcomes.
@audit_trail.purpose: Enables accountability, debugging, and pattern detection.

@allowlist.definition: A set of pre-approved actions, commands, or resources that bypass full audit.
examples: Safe shell commands: ls, pwd, echo, cat (read-only)
@allowlist.maintenance: Allowlists should be minimal and reviewed regularly.
@allowlist.note: Presence on allowlist skips LLM audit but still logs to audit_trail.

@denylist.definition: A set of always-blocked patterns that trigger immediate BLOCK verdict.
examples: Destructive patterns: rm -rf, format, dd if=
Exfiltration patterns: curl * | bash, base64 encode + send
@denylist.note: Denylist match triggers BLOCK without LLM consultation for speed.
